raw_meta_yaml:
# handle undefined PYTHON in `noarch: generic` outputs
schema_version: 1

context:
  version: "30.18.0"
  PYTHON: $PYTHON
  # sqlglotc is compiled with a private mypy fork (same PyPI description/import
  # names as stock mypy) published by upstream to build sqlglotc independently
  # of the upstream mypy release cadence; it is packaged separately on
  # conda-forge and used only as sqlglotc's host build tool.
  sqlglot_mypy_version: "2.3.0.post2"
  py_bin: ${{ "so" if unix else "pyd" }}

recipe:
  name: sqlglot
  version: ${{ version }}

build:
  number: 0

outputs:
  - package:
      name: sqlglot
    source:
      url: https://pypi.org/packages/source/s/sqlglot/sqlglot-${{ version }}.tar.gz
      sha256: e57e1b205e341979d1df5b1212c1435c598a0437e4619e3f428b15d5bc3a5cc6
    build:
      noarch: python
      script: ${{ PYTHON }} -m pip install . -vv --no-deps --no-build-isolation --disable-pip-version-check
    requirements:
      host:
        - pip
        - python ${{ python_min }}.*
        - setuptools_scm
        - setuptools >=61.0
      run:
        - python >=${{ python_min }}
    tests:
      - python:
          imports:
            - sqlglot
          pip_check: true
          python_version:
            - ${{ python_min }}.*
            - "*"
      - files:
          source:
            - tests/
        requirements:
          run:
            - openjdk
            - pandas
            - pip
            - pyspark
            - pytest
            - python-dateutil
            - python-duckdb >=0.6
            - python ${{ python_min }}.*
            - pytz
        script:
          # On Windows, Python's stdout defaults to the console's legacy
          # codepage rather than UTF-8; pytest's tee/color output then emits
          # bytes rattler-build's log reader can't decode as UTF-8, aborting
          # the test step even though every test passed. Force UTF-8 mode.
          # cmd.exe's `set` does not trim trailing whitespace, so the value
          # must butt directly up against `&&` or PYTHONUTF8 ends up as "1 "
          # (with a trailing space), which Python's strict parser rejects.
          - ${{ "set PYTHONUTF8=1&& set PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8&& " if win else "" }}pytest -vvv --capture=tee-sys --color=yes --tb=long tests

  - package:
      name: sqlglotc
      version: ${{ version }}
    source:
      - url: https://pypi.org/packages/source/s/sqlglotc/sqlglotc-${{ version }}.tar.gz
        sha256: 3f0767b30aa96a45d7560df113c5ff2be1b98c69e6cb6c84cd3fbd1c8dc0e25d
      # sqlglotc's sdist ships no LICENSE file; pull the matching tag's from
      # the tobymao/sqlglot monorepo the sqlglotc/ subdirectory is cut from.
      - url: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tobymao/sqlglot/v${{ version }}/LICENSE
        file_name: LICENSE
        sha256: b0bf909b472ddf9bd4eab30f6e6fd8b33bf3997ce038b882fe0663f291958d2d
    build:
      number: 0
      script:
        - ${{ PYTHON }} -m pip install . --no-deps -vv --no-build-isolation --disable-pip-version-check
    requirements:
      build:
        - ${{ compiler("c") }}
        - ${{ stdlib("c") }}
      host:
        - pip
        - python
        - setuptools >=61.0
        - setuptools_scm
        - sqlglot-mypy ==${{ sqlglot_mypy_version }}
        - types-python-dateutil
        # sqlglotc's pyproject.toml lists sqlglot under [build-system], and
        # both are cut from the same tobymao/sqlglot tag/version, so pin to
        # the sqlglot output built in this same recipe rather than a
        # standalone version constraint.
        - ${{ pin_subpackage("sqlglot", lower_bound='x.x.x', upper_bound='x.x.x') }}
      run:
        - python
        - ${{ pin_subpackage("sqlglot", lower_bound='x.x.x', upper_bound='x.x.x') }}
    tests:
      - python:
          imports:
            - sqlglot
          pip_check: true
      - package_contents:
          site_packages:
            - sqlglot/parser*.${{ py_bin }}
            - sqlglot/tokenizer_core*.${{ py_bin }}
            - sqlglot/expressions/core*.${{ py_bin }}
      - script:
          # sqlglotc has no importable API of its own: it drops compiled
          # modules into sqlglot's own package directory, and CPython's
          # default import order prefers extension modules over the .py
          # source of the same name, so this confirms the accelerator
          # actually got picked up at runtime.
          - python -c "import sqlglot.parser as p; assert not p.__file__.endswith('.py'), p.__file__"
    about:
      summary: mypyc-compiled extensions for sqlglot
      description: |
        sqlglotc ships mypyc-compiled native extensions for sqlglot, the SQL
        parser and transpiler. Installing it drops compiled `.so`/`.pyd`
        modules directly into the already-installed `sqlglot` package's
        directories (tokenizer, parser, generator, optimizer, and every SQL
        dialect's generator/parser), which Python's import machinery prefers
        over the interpreted `.py` sources, giving a significant parsing and
        generation speedup with no code changes required. sqlglotc carries no
        Python API of its own and no functionality beyond the compiled
        modules; each sqlglotc release is pinned to and must be installed
        alongside the exact matching sqlglot release.
      license: MIT
      license_file: LICENSE
      homepage: https://sqlglot.com/
      repository: https://github.com/tobymao/sqlglot
      documentation: https://sqlglot.com/

about:
  summary: An easily customizable SQL parser and transpiler
  license: MIT
  license_file: LICENSE
  homepage: https://github.com/tobymao/sqlglot

extra:
  recipe-maintainers:
    - timkpaine
    - tobymao
    - thewchan
    - pb01ka
